source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1/supply-chain-diversification-benefit narrative found; conversely, Sun Pharma is expanding INTO China via a new wholly-owned subsidiary (Sun Pharma Hainan, incorporated Jul 2025) and a partnership with China Medical System Holdings to access Chinese distribution channels — the opposite framing of the China+1 thesis.

inr_exposure.evidence: Segment revenues (US, Emerging Markets, Rest of World, Global Specialty) are reported in USD by the company (e.g. US $1,921mn, Emerging Markets $1,114mn, RoW $847mn, Global Specialty $1,216mn in FY25), implying material USD revenue exposure, but no explicit consolidated USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy text was retrievable.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma is one of 55 companies selected under India's Rs 15,000 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for pharmaceuticals, placed in Group A (largest manufacturers) alongside Dr Reddy's and Cipla. No specific revenue or margin contribution figure from PLI was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: IKS is a healthcare BPO/services company (not a goods manufacturer/exporter); no China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative found in any source reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carried acquisition-related debt (~INR 856 cr as of Mar-2025, down from ~INR 1,311 cr a year earlier) tied to the AQuity acquisition; gearing reported at 0.47x in FY25 improving to 0.27x in FY26. Floating vs fixed split not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources describe IKS Health's revenue as overwhelmingly US-client-derived (one source: ~100% international; another: >90% of revenue from the US), consistent with its role as a healthcare BPO serving US physician groups/hospitals. No exact company-disclosed USD-revenue % or hedging policy verified from primary AR.

pli_scheme.evidence: PLI schemes apply to manufacturing sectors; IKS is a services/BPO company and no PLI mention was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Q4 FY25 earnings call: exports in the mobility aftermarket business grew ~17% YoY with notable improvement in Nepal, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka; management described an 'international production network' model (production sited near consumption, e.g. Europe for Europe, India for India) with exports covering shortfalls/extra demand, citing NOx Sensor production at the Bidadi plant being exported back to Europe, and stated intent to keep increasing export share. No explicit 'China+1' phrase found.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural revenue % disclosed. Qualitative: Alkem has strong rural/tier-2-3 distribution via in-house field force; trade-generics segment (skewed rural/semi-urban) was ~Rs 2,400 cr of ~Rs 8,100 cr domestic revenue in FY23 (~30% of domestic sales) per Forbes India profile.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export sales were ~29.8% of FY25 total revenue (India ~Rs 8,983.7 cr vs international ~Rs 3,821 cr); US generics declined ~15% YoY in H1FY25 due to price erosion/supply issues. Exact USD-denominated % and hedging policy not found.

rural.evidence: Secondary sources reference NH's NGO partnerships and free medical camps in rural areas as part of outreach/CSR activity, but no quantified rural revenue % was found; primary AR text could not be accessed to confirm.

govt_capex.evidence: NH hospitals are empanelled under Ayushman Bharat/PM-JAY (govt health insurance scheme), implying some govt-scheme-linked patient revenue, but no explicit % of revenue disclosure was found in accessible sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: NH's Health City Cayman Islands hospital (~21.6% of FY25 consolidated revenue: Cayman revenue ~INR 11,829 Mn of ~INR 54,830 Mn total per secondary financial data aggregators) serves largely US-origin medical tourism patients and likely generates USD-linked revenue, but exact USD revenue % and hedging policy from the AR's financial risk management note could not be verified since the primary Annual Report PDF and company IR site were unreachable.

pli_scheme.evidence: NH is a hospital/healthcare services operator, not a manufacturer; PLI schemes apply to manufacturing sectors, and no mention of NH as a PLI beneficiary was found.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification narrative; Usha Martin's international presence is its own long-standing global manufacturing footprint (plants/JVs in UK, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Dubai, Australia), not customers shifting sourcing away from China.

govt_capex.evidence: News coverage of FY25 results: international markets were 55% of FY25 revenue, 'reflecting sustained demand in sectors such as oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure' — meaningful exposure to govt/public-capex-linked end markets (mining, infra), but no quantified revenue share by end-market found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is steel wire rod, not crude oil/petroleum derivatives — not applicable.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export sales were 55% of FY25 consolidated revenue (₹3,474 cr total), implying material FX revenue exposure; exact USD-denominated share and hedging policy not accessible.

FY25 (year ended Mar-2025) consolidated revenue was ~Rs 3,918 cr, split Domestic Rs 2,269 cr (58%) vs International (Russia/CIS branded formulations, other export branded generics, CDMO, API) Rs 1,649 cr (42%), per segment data reported in press coverage of results. Within the international bucket: International formulations Rs 1,128 cr, CDMO Rs 446 cr, API Rs 76 cr. Implies material non-INR revenue/receivables exposure (Russia/CIS in RUB, Africa in ZAR, branded generics/CDMO likely partly USD), but exact currency-wise split and hedging policy could not be confirmed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative found. Radico's export story (Rampur Single Malt, Jaisalmer Gin reaching 85-100+ countries incl. US, Europe, Middle East, SE Asia) is premiumization-led, not a China+1 manufacturing-relocation play, consistent with alcobev being a non-manufacturing-diversification sector.

rural.evidence: Secondary sources describe a pan-India network of 60,000-100,000+ retail outlets with explicit emphasis on semi-urban/rural penetration for mass IMFL brands (8PM Whisky, Contessa Rum, Old Admiral Brandy), and cite rising rural incomes/agri spending as a demand driver for mass/mid-premium segments. No explicit rural revenue % was disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary inputs cited are grain/molasses-based ENA (extra neutral alcohol) and glass/PET packaging; no crude-oil-linked cost commentary was found in the sources accessible during this research.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to 85-100+ countries (US, Europe, Middle East, Southeast Asia) but export revenue as a % of total revenue, and any forex hedging policy, were not found in the sources accessed.

rural.evidence: NIMF's AUM from 'Beyond the Top 30 cities' (B-30) stood at Rs 1.32 trillion, up 15% YoY, forming 19.8% of NIMF's total AUM versus an industry average of 18.6%, per FY24-25 company disclosures. This is an AUM penetration metric (standard AMC disclosure proxy for smaller-city/rural-adjacent reach), not a strict revenue split.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No literal floating-rate liability % disclosed (AMC, not a borrower-heavy balance sheet). Rate-cut sensitivity narrative: RBI cut the repo rate by 25bps to 6.25% in Q4 FY25, with the 10-year G-Sec yield down 18bps QoQ to 6.58%; easing rate environment linked to stronger debt/fixed-income fund performance and flows, with NIMF's quarterly SIP flows rising 19.9% QoQ to Rs 90.3 billion in the same period. Management also flagged structural yield/margin pressure of 1-2bps/year from higher distribution costs and growth in lower-margin ETF/debt AUM mix.

inr_exposure.evidence: NAM-India has two wholly-owned overseas subsidiaries (Singapore, Mauritius) plus a Dubai representative office, managing offshore UCITS equity/fixed-income funds, an India Fixed Income ETF, and segregated mandates for institutional/HNI investors across Asia, Middle East, UK, US, Latin America and Europe. No specific % of consolidated revenue/AUM attributable to overseas or foreign-currency sources, nor any hedging policy, was found disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative found in accessible sources; company exports ~10% of revenue (likely largely intra-ABB-Group) but no diversification angle was documented in the excerpts retrieved.

govt_capex.evidence: Qualitative disclosure (no hard percentage) attributes order momentum to government capex: 'the government's capital expenditure focus on new-age themes such as energy efficiency, decarbonization, and digitalization, has significantly driven order momentum'; also 'Higher capex in infrastructure, railways, renewables, power distribution, water, energy, commercial buildings, and metals are likely to provide necessary opportunities for growth.' ABB India is described as a key supplier of railway propulsion technology and a participant in India's power-grid buildout (with Hitachi Energy India, Siemens Energy). CY2024 total orders were INR 13,079 crore, with growth from data centers and railways segments.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export share (~10% of revenue, per FY2023 disclosure) implies some USD/EUR exposure, but no specific currency breakdown or hedging policy statement was found in accessible sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found that ABB India participates in any PLI scheme; PLI schemes found in search results target electronics/mobile/semiconductor manufacturing, not ABB India's electrification/automation/robotics segments.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Net debt reportedly reduced to ~INR 25,000 million in FY25 from ~INR 46,000 million in FY23 (broker note, HDFC Securities), largely from Curatio-acquisition-related borrowings; specific floating-vs-fixed rate split not accessible in sources retrieved.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has multi-currency revenue exposure: US ~10% of FY25 revenue, Germany ~10% (EUR), Brazil ~10% (BRL); specific hedging policy disclosure not accessible in sources retrieved.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Phoenix Mills' FY25 earnings calls (Q2/Q3/Q4 FY25) report cost of debt falling from 9.2% to 8.5% over FY25 as RBI rate cuts flowed through the company's lease-rental-discounting/project-finance loan book (gross debt ~INR 4,400 crore, net debt/EBITDA 1.2x); Q1 FY26 cost of debt fell further to ~7.92%, with management noting further RBI rate cuts would continue to reprice the loan portfolio downward — indicating a largely floating/MCLR-linked debt structure, though the AR itself was not directly accessible to confirm an exact floating-rate percentage.

rural.evidence: Zydus Lifesciences' Consumer Wellness segment (Complan, Sugar Free, Glucon-D, Nycil — ~14-18% of consolidated revenue) derives roughly 50% of its store presence from rural/small-town outlets, with sachetization driving ~25% of segment sales, per investor commentary. No company-wide 'rural revenue %' figure was found disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: US Formulations business alone contributes roughly 35-47% of consolidated revenue (figures vary by quarter/source: Q1 FY25 ~51%, full-year FY25 investor deck ~35.2%), implying material USD-denominated revenue, but no explicit 'USD revenue %' or hedging policy disclosure could be retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: Could not confirm Zydus Lifesciences (Cadila Healthcare) as an approved applicant on India's PLI scheme for Bulk Drugs/APIs or Pharmaceuticals via available sources; not found in searched approved-applicant lists or company disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Secondary sources describe Sona Comstar as India's largest importer of rare-earth (NdFeB) magnets from China for its EV traction motor business, and report it halted a China JV amid 2025 rare-earth export curbs, prompting plans to build domestic magnet manufacturing capacity (backed by a proposed ~Rs 7,300 crore government PLI scheme) to cut China import dependency. This is an import-substitution/supply-risk narrative, not a confirmed AR statement that export customers are diversifying orders away from Chinese suppliers toward Sona Comstar (the classic China+1 export-demand story), so strength is marked weak/uncertain rather than moderate or strong.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are steel/forgings and rare-earth (NdFeB) magnets, not crude-oil-linked inputs; no crude/commodity-price disclosure of this type found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary sources state ~76% of revenue comes from international/export sales (multi-currency, likely USD- and EUR-heavy given North America/Europe EV customers), and the company has manufacturing plants in the US, Mexico and China providing a partial natural hedge. Specific USD-only revenue % and formal hedging policy language were not retrieved.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar became the first Indian auto-component supplier to receive Auto PLI scheme certification (for its hub-wheel-drive motor for e-two-wheelers) and has filed seven applications for different products under the scheme. It is also positioning to participate in the government's separate proposed ~Rs 7,300 crore Rare Earth Magnet PLI scheme for domestic NdFeB magnet manufacturing. No specific incentive amount or revenue % contribution was disclosed.

rural.evidence: Search snippets on Nykaa's FY2024-25 Integrated Annual Report indicate Tier-II/III geographies are growing faster than Tier-I, and roughly half of the 50 new stores opened in FY25 were in Tier-II/III cities; separately, Nykaa Now (quick commerce) sourced over 90% of its contribution from India's top 8 metro/tier-1 cities as of the FY25 concall period. No explicit rural/Tier-2-3 revenue percentage for total company revenue was found; primary AR PDF could not be fetched.

inr_exposure.evidence: Owned brand Kay Beauty was reported (via secondary press coverage) to have launched at Space NK in the UK in FY25, but no export revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed in any accessible source.

govt_capex.evidence: Africa Institutional business (anti-malarial supply via government/NGO tenders, ~9% of FY24 sales) is tender-driven but this is not domestic government capex exposure; no disclosure of India government capex linkage found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Brokerage commentary (Dolat Capital FY24 AR analysis) noted material cost of ~Rs 832 crore in FY22 with ~Rs 700 crore third-party sourced APIs, and margin pressure from 'elevated API prices'; no specific crude-oil-linked raw material percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company uses forex derivative contracts to hedge export receivables; reported forex derivative losses (e.g., ~Rs 37 crore in Q3 FY23) flowing through other expenses, indicating an active but not fully effective hedging program.
inr_exposure.evidence: ~69% of FY24 consolidated sales came from exports (US, Asia, Africa branded + Africa institutional), which are predominantly USD-invoiced, though no explicit 'USD revenue %' figure was disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No disclosure found of Ajanta Pharma participating in the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for bulk drugs/APIs; PLI benefits in Indian pharma are concentrated among API/KSM-focused manufacturers, and Ajanta is a formulations/branded-generics-focused company.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt fell to ₹255.11 cr (Mar-2025) from ₹766.60 cr (Mar-2024) after IPO proceeds (Jul-2024) were used to repay borrowings; no floating vs fixed-rate split was disclosed in sources reviewed (secondary press/rating-agency coverage, not primary AR notes).

inr_exposure.evidence: Company is reported to offset foreign-currency payables (trade obligations, loans) against foreign-currency receivables from exports, creating a natural hedge; no explicit forward-contract hedging percentage or USD-revenue-specific disclosure was located.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals was one of 9 companies approved under Group B of the Government's PLI Scheme for Key Starting Materials (KSMs)/Drug Intermediates/APIs (alongside MSN Labs, Wockhardt, Alembic, Macleods, Biological E, Natco, Strides). No revenue contribution percentage from the scheme was found.
